question.problem:
In **ascending order**, the solutions to $4{g}^{2}=\frac{2g}{5}$ are $g=${{field-1}} and $g=$
{{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we move all of the terms to the left-hand side and then factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{g}^{2} & =\frac{2g}{5} \\ 4{g}^{2}-\frac{2g}{5} & =0 \\ 2g(2g-\frac{1}{5}) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the zero product rule to get

$$
2g=0\,\text{or}\,2g-\frac{1}{5}=0,
$$

which in turn gives

$$
g=0\,\text{or}\,g=\frac{1}{10}.
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $g=0$ and $g=\frac{1}{10}.$
